assessments.reasoning: XPath 3.1 production 69 makes the entire entry list optional. When present, it starts with one entry and allows further entries after commas. Productions 70–72 require an ExprSingle on each side of the entry’s colon.

challenge.method: Test empty braces, a trailing comma, and a colon that could be consumed as part of a qualified name.
challenge.results: Empty braces are permitted. A comma at entry-list level requires a following entry. Longest-match tokenization can absorb a colon into a name, so whitespace can determine whether an entry parses. Syntactic permission alone establishes no evaluation result.

limitations: Lexical treatment of colons applies. Grammar alone does not guarantee successful evaluation of a constructor.
Syntax permission does not establish successful key or value evaluation.
